title: Streamlined v2 hero visuals and step-card pattern
creator: Aisha Malik
description: Goal: Redesign the Quickstart landing hero and the supporting step-card pattern to reduce cognitive load, improve scan-ability, and create reusable assets for docs and release screenshots. Scope includes hero art (static + Lottie micro-animation), responsive breakpoints, three step-card templates (onboarding flow, integration checklist, troubleshooting), updated microcopy, and an automated screenshot workflow for the release pipeline. Out of scope: backend onboarding logic and MD content; separate ticket will cover copy localization.
acceptance_criteria: Hero visually matches new brand scale and sits under 420px height at 1200px viewport without truncation
Step-card templates render correctly at three breakpoints (mobile, tablet, desktop) and pass contrast ratio >=4.5:1
Figma master components and variants delivered with documentation and tokens for spacing, typography, and elevation
Automated screenshot script added to the release repo that can render hero + step-cards in headless Chrome and output PNGs for docs and marketing
Accessibility pass: keyboard focus states documented and 3 sample screen-reader labels included
design_notes: We are moving away from dense multi-column hero to a single-column centered hero with optional right-aligned preview pane. The hero preview will be a simplified app mock that supports a Lottie micro-animation for token streaming. Step-cards should use a modular grid with two visual weights: primary (action on the left + short body) and neutral (icon + summary). Use the new 'Nebula' token palette for highlights and keep CTA to a single primary action. Avoid illustrative hero scenes that imply specific product flows.
deliverables: Figma file: /redwood/quickstart/streamlined-v2 with component library and master frames
Design spec doc in Confluence with spacing tokens and accessibility notes
